After installing Modeler 14.1 64-bit client and Statistics 32-bit client on a 64-bit operating system, Modeler cannot find the Statistics install. Nor will any of the Statistics function within Modeler. The user will receive the error "Please run the Statistics License Utility"


RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
 

Having a 64-bit install of Modeler and a 32-bit installation of Statistics is not a supported configuration by IBM SPSS. In order to use the SPSS Statistics nodes from within Modeler, you will need to install the 64-bit version of Statistics. To resolve the StaleConnectionException in WebSphere Application Server, you can follow these steps:

1. Configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool to eliminate occurrences of StaleConnectionException. 
   * Set the Minimum connections to 0 to avoid situations where a connection is kept in the pool to meet the minimum requirement, even though it may have been idle for longer than Unused timeout.
   * Set the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that the sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout.

2. If you are using the JCC driver, ensure you are using version 3.59.81 or later, which was shipped with DB2 v9.5fp6a or later and DB2 v9.7fp2 or later. This version incorporates a fix for the StaleConnectionException issue (defect 134363).

3. As a workaround for the JCC driver issue, you can add "COMMIT ON RETURN YES" to the definition of the stored procedure on the host.

4. Reduce the Minimum Connections to 0 on the data source. This will cause WAS to remove all connections after a period of inactivity. 
   * In the WAS admin console, go to Resources -> JDBC -> Data sources.
   * For each of the db domains, select the Connection pools link and edit the Minimum connection folder.
   * Restart the servers after the changes are made.

Note: Reviewing the Portal's systemOut.log may help diagnose the problem, as the stale connection exception will be visible when attempting to access the database. 

Additionally, the error codes and SQL states provided in the question, such as ORA-02396 and 61000, Error Code = 2,396, may indicate that the issue is related to exceeded maximum idle time or not being logged on, which can be addressed by adjusting the connection pool settings as described above.

IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases provide sharing conversations (SHARECNV) attribute on SVRCONN channel that specifies the maximum number of conversations that can share each TCP/IP channel instance. This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel. The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object. The same default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is 
negotiated between MQ server and DataPower and the lower value takes effect. However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server.

However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server. There are three use cases to configure Sharing Conversations in DataPower mq-qm object: 

Case #1 : The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0 - The channel runs in a mode similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not uses features such as

· Administrator stop-quiesce
· Heartbeating 
· Read ahead 
· Client asynchronous consume

Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower to disable sharing conversations regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting. Case #2: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 1 - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features as outlined in case #1, but each TCP/IP channel instance has a single conversation.

Case #3: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features and each TCP/IP channel instance supports 2 or more conversations. Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower and on the MQ SVRCONN channel. Since DataPower uses a connection pool in processing MQ messages, there are no additional benefits of using sharing conversations with the mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call. When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call. However, when mixed message sizes are processed by the same MQ Front Side Handler (FSH), it requests buffer pool based on maximum message size configured in the mq-qm object.

6. **Special Values on DataPower**: Be aware that in current versions of the DataPower firmware, a sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with the MQ server.
